items.summary: Qatar and Pakistan proposed that Iran receive the interest earned on ~$6B of Iranian funds frozen in Qatari banks in exchange for a confidential, unannounced IAEA visit to Iranian nuclear facilities — first reported by The New Arab on Tuesday, Oct 20. Pakistan's army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir conveyed the proposal to Iranian officials during his Tehran visit (he also discussed mediation with President Pezeshkian, per Nournews). Sources say Washington and Tehran responded positively, though neither government publicly confirmed. Separately, Qatari foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari confirmed in Doha on Tuesday that Qatar/Oman/Pakistan mediation remains active with drafts being exchanged between the capitals.
items.title: Qatar, Pakistan propose $6B-interest-for-IAEA-inspections compromise deal

items.event_time_ist: Oct 20, 2026 (date known; exact time not published)
items.summary: FM Abbas Araghchi said Tuesday that indirect negotiations with the US are continuing via Pakistan and Qatar, but the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until Washington accepts Iran's terms and honours its MoU commitments. Under Iran's Seven-Day Plan, the strait was to be fully reopened on day six; Araghchi said Washington had signalled agreement but then sought to add new conditions. On X he warned final-deal negotiations 'will not commence if threats continue,' invoking MoU paragraph 13. He also asserted the strait lies entirely in Iranian and Omani territorial waters and that only the Iran-Oman agreed route would be used if it reopens.
items.title: Araghchi: Hormuz stays closed until America accepts Iran's conditions
